natural: a pointed head and darting eyes

meaning.en: Describes an ugly, shifty-looking person, as if of bad character.
meaning.zh: 形容人相貌丑陋、神情狡猾，让人觉得不是好人。

examples.zh: 这个獐头鼠目的家伙，一看就不老实。
examples.en: That weaselly-looking fellow clearly can't be trusted.

examples.zh: 小说里的反派往往被描写成獐头鼠目的样子。
examples.en: Villains in novels are often described as shifty-looking.

examples.zh: 别以貌取人，獐头鼠目的人未必是坏人。
examples.en: Don't judge by appearances; a shifty-looking man isn't necessarily a bad one.

usage.en: Derogatory and colloquial, about looks. Note 獐 is zhāng ('river deer'), often mistyped as 章. Judging character by looks is itself frowned on.
usage.zh: 贬义，口语，指相貌。“獐”读 zhāng，常被误写成“章”。以貌取人本身并不可取。

natural: the effort of blowing off dust

meaning.en: A very slight effort; mostly in the negative: without the least effort.
meaning.zh: 吹掉灰尘那样微小的力气；多用于否定式，表示毫不费力。

examples.zh: 这道题对他来说不费吹灰之力。
examples.en: The question took him no effort at all.

examples.zh: 要拿下这个客户，可不是不费吹灰之力的事。
examples.en: Winning this client won't be effortless.

examples.zh: 他不费吹灰之力就赢了比赛。
examples.en: He won the match without breaking a sweat.

usage.en: Almost always in 不费吹灰之力 or 毫不费吹灰之力. In a positive sentence it is rare and needs 只/仅 for 'just that little effort'.
usage.zh: 几乎总是说“不费吹灰之力”。肯定句很少见，需要搭配“只、仅”。

natural: Mr Nice Guy

meaning.en: A person who agrees with everyone and avoids taking a stand to stay on good terms.
meaning.zh: 指不讲原则、与人无争、谁都不得罪的人。

equivalents: someone who never takes a side

examples.zh: 他是个好好先生，从不拒绝任何人。
examples.en: He's a Mr Nice Guy who never says no to anyone.

examples.zh: 当领导不能当好好先生，该批评时要批评。
examples.en: A leader can't be a yes-man; criticism has to be given when due.

examples.zh: 会上他谁都不得罪，真是个好好先生。
examples.en: At the meeting he offended nobody, a real pushover.

usage.en: Mildly derogatory. Differs from 老好人 (which can be neutral) in highlighting a lack of principle. Noun phrase.
usage.zh: 略带贬义，强调没有原则；与“老好人”相比，后者有时是中性。名词性。

natural: are you well since we parted?

meaning.en: A greeting to someone long unseen: hope you have been well since we parted.
meaning.zh: 分别以来一向可好；用于问候久别的人。

equivalents: how have you been since we last met?

examples.zh: 多年不见，别来无恙？
examples.en: Long time no see; how have you been?

examples.zh: 老同学重逢，第一句话便是“别来无恙”。
examples.en: When old classmates met again, the first thing said was 'I hope you've been well'.

examples.zh: 先生别来无恙，风采依旧。
examples.en: I hope you've been well, sir; you look just as splendid.

usage.en: A greeting, somewhat literary or playful in modern speech. Don't use it for people you see regularly. 恙 is read yàng.
usage.zh: 问候语，现代口语中略带书面或戏谑色彩。常见面的人不适用。“恙”读 yàng。

natural: hiding treasure deep, as if there were none

meaning.en: To be modest and conceal real ability or knowledge so that one seems to have little.
meaning.zh: 把珍宝藏得很深，好像没有一样；比喻有才学而不外露。

examples.zh: 真正的高手往往深藏若虚。
examples.en: Real masters are often modest and keep their skills hidden.

examples.zh: 他深藏若虚，没人知道他是个专家。
examples.en: He was so unassuming that nobody knew he was an expert.

examples.zh: 做人要深藏若虚，不要处处炫耀。
examples.en: One should be unassuming rather than show off at every turn.

story.en: Laozi told Confucius that a good merchant hides his goods deep as if he had none, and a gentleman with full virtue looks like a fool.
story.zh: 老子对孔子说：“吾闻之，良贾深藏若虚，君子盛德，容貌若愚。”

usage.en: Praise of modesty; often paired with 大智若愚. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 褒义，赞美谦虚；常与“大智若愚”连用。作谓语、定语。

natural: seeing the small and knowing the large

meaning.en: To foresee how things will develop from small signs.
meaning.zh: 从细微的苗头预见事物的发展趋势。

equivalents: see the big picture in small details

examples.zh: 好的医生能见微知著，早期发现病情。
examples.en: A good doctor can read small signs and spot illness early.

examples.zh: 他见微知著，提前预判了市场变化。
examples.en: He read the signs and anticipated the market shift.

examples.zh: 见微知著，从孩子的小习惯可看出他的性格。
examples.en: Small habits show a child's character.

story.en: Han Feizi says the sage sees the slight and knows the sprout, sees the beginning and knows the end.
story.zh: 《韩非子·说林上》：“圣人见微以知萌，见端以知末。”

usage.en: Praise of insight; formal. Often paired with 防微杜渐. 著 is read zhù ('obvious').
usage.zh: 褒义，赞美洞察力；较正式，常与“防微杜渐”连用。“著”读 zhù。

natural: an oily manner of speaking

meaning.en: Speaking in a glib, flippant way that is not sincere or serious.
meaning.zh: 形容人说话轻浮油滑，不诚恳、不严肃。

examples.zh: 他说话油腔滑调，让人不敢信任。
examples.en: He talks glibly and people can't trust him.

examples.zh: 销售员油腔滑调的推销，让顾客反感。
examples.en: The salesman's slick patter annoyed customers.

examples.zh: 正式场合别油腔滑调的。
examples.en: Don't be flippant on formal occasions.

usage.en: Derogatory, about someone's speaking manner. 腔 is qiāng. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 贬义，指说话态度。“腔”读 qiāng。作谓语、定语。

natural: the soul no longer attached to the body

meaning.en: So terrified that one is scarcely aware of oneself.
meaning.zh: 吓得魂魄都离开了身体；形容极度惊恐，失去常态。

examples.zh: 听到巨响，孩子吓得魂不附体。
examples.en: The child was scared out of his wits by the bang.

examples.zh: 遇上劫匪，她魂不附体，说不出话来。
examples.en: Facing the robbers she was frozen with fear and couldn't speak.

examples.zh: 这场车祸让他魂不附体。
examples.en: The crash left him scared witless.

usage.en: Describes fright; also 魂飞魄散 (stronger). Predicate or complement, e.g. 吓得魂不附体. 附 is fù.
usage.zh: 形容惊恐；与“魂飞魄散”近，后者更强烈。作谓语、补语，如“吓得魂不附体”。“附”读 fù。

natural: peeping through a tube and measuring with a ladle

meaning.en: To view or judge things from a narrow perspective; also a modest way to call one's own view shallow.
meaning.zh: 从竹管里看天，用瓢测海；比喻见识狭窄、观察片面，也用作自谦。

examples.zh: 以上只是管窥蠡测，不当之处请指正。
examples.en: This is only my limited view; please correct any errors.

examples.zh: 仅凭一两个例子下结论，不过是管窥蠡测。
examples.en: Drawing conclusions from one or two examples is a very narrow view.

examples.zh: 对如此复杂的问题，我们的研究只是管窥蠡测。
examples.en: On so complex an issue our research is only a partial glimpse.

story.en: Dongfang Shuo, answering a critic, says that to peep at the sky through a tube and measure the sea with a gourd ladle is to fail to know the whole.
story.zh: 东方朔《答客难》：“以管窥天，以蠡测海，以莛撞钟，岂能通其条贯，考其文理，发其音声哉！”

usage.en: Literary; used about others as criticism and about oneself as modesty. 蠡 is read lí (a gourd ladle) in this idiom, and 测 means to measure.
usage.zh: 书面语；批评别人，或用于自谦。此处“蠡”读 lí，指瓢。

natural: to die by the law one has made

meaning.en: To be caught out by one's own scheme or rules; to suffer from what one devised.
meaning.zh: 自己订立的法令或设计的计策，反而使自己受害。

equivalents: fall victim to one's own rules

examples.zh: 他设下的圈套，最后让自己作法自毙。
examples.en: The trap he set ended up catching him.

examples.zh: 这项条款最后让起草者作法自毙。
examples.en: The clause ended up being the drafters' own undoing.

examples.zh: 制定规则的人也要遵守，否则可能作法自毙。
examples.en: Rule-makers must follow them too, or they may be hoist with their own petard.

story.en: Shang Yang fled and tried to stay at an inn, but the innkeeper refused him as the law he had made forbade lodging someone without papers; he sighed at the disaster the law had brought.
story.zh: 商鞅逃至客舍，客舍人不知他是商君，说商君之法不许留宿无证之人；商鞅叹曰：“嗟乎，为法之敝一至此哉！”

usage.en: Describes a case of poetic justice. Mostly predicate; 毙 is bì ('die'). Often confused with 作茧自缚, which is more about self-entrapment.
usage.zh: 描述咎由自取的情形，多作谓语；“毙”读 bì。常与“作茧自缚”混淆，后者更强调自我束缚。

natural: a face the colour of earth

meaning.en: A face turned pale and ashen from fright, shock or illness.
meaning.zh: 脸色像泥土一样灰暗，形容极度惊恐或受惊吓的样子。

examples.zh: 听到噩耗，她顿时面如土色。
examples.en: On hearing the terrible news she turned ashen.

examples.zh: 考官宣布成绩时，他面如土色。
examples.en: When the examiner announced the results he went pale.

examples.zh: 他吓得面如土色，半天说不出话。
examples.en: He was so frightened that his face went grey and he was speechless for a long while.

usage.en: Describes the face under shock; may also describe sickness. Predicate or complement.
usage.zh: 描写受惊时的脸色，也可指病容。作谓语、补语。

natural: the more you say, the more slips you make

meaning.en: The more one talks, the more likely one is to say something wrong.
meaning.zh: 话说得多了，难免出错。

equivalents: the more you talk, the more you slip

examples.zh: 言多必失，在谈判中少说为妙。
examples.en: The more you say, the more mistakes you make, so say little in negotiations.

examples.zh: 他喝了酒话多，言多必失，说漏了秘密。
examples.en: Drunk and talkative, he let a secret slip.

examples.zh: 记住言多必失，关键场合要谨慎发言。
examples.en: Remember that talking too much brings errors, so speak carefully on crucial occasions.

usage.en: Advice for caution in speech; often used as a sigh after a slip. Close to 祸从口出 but milder.
usage.zh: 劝人说话谨慎，说错话后常用来感叹。与“祸从口出”近，但程度较轻。

natural: busy with war horses

meaning.en: Describes the busy, hurried life of soldiers at war.
meaning.zh: 形容军事活动繁忙紧张。

examples.zh: 他戎马倥偬数十年，才得以解甲归田。
examples.en: He spent decades on military campaigns before being able to retire.

examples.zh: 在戎马倥偬的岁月里，他依然坚持读书。
examples.en: Through the busy years of war he kept up his reading.

examples.zh: 这位将军戎马倥偬，一生南征北战。
examples.en: The general spent his life campaigning north and south.

usage.en: Literary, about a soldier's career; 倥偬 is kǒng zǒng ('pressed, urgent'). Not for modern military in routine settings.
usage.zh: 书面语，写军人生涯；“倥偬”读 kǒng zǒng，意为紧迫繁忙。

natural: not enough to get things done

meaning.en: Unable to accomplish anything; usually 'better at spoiling things than finishing them'.
meaning.zh: 办不成事，反而常常把事情搞坏（常与“败事有余”连用）。

equivalents: more of a hindrance than a help

examples.zh: 成事不足，败事有余，有他在反而添乱。
examples.en: He is no help and an expert at spoiling things; having him around only adds trouble.

examples.zh: 他成事不足，却爱指手画脚。
examples.en: He can't get anything done, yet he loves to give orders.

examples.zh: 别找这种成事不足的人合作。
examples.en: Don't partner with someone who is useless at getting things done.

usage.en: Normally quoted as 成事不足，败事有余. Derogatory, colloquial.
usage.zh: 通常说“成事不足，败事有余”。贬义，口语。

natural: lingering feelings of love

meaning.en: Absorbed in romantic or family affection, often implying a lack of larger ambition.
meaning.zh: 指过分沉溺于男女恋情或家庭情感。

equivalents: too absorbed in romance and family

examples.zh: 大丈夫志在四方，不可儿女情长。
examples.en: A man of ambition aims for the world and should not be too wrapped up in sentiment.

examples.zh: 他不是儿女情长的人，工作永远排在第一位。
examples.en: He isn't sentimental; work always comes first.

examples.zh: 儿女情长，英雄气短。
examples.en: Fondness for love saps heroic spirit.

usage.en: Usually in the pattern 儿女情长，英雄气短. Mild criticism, though also describes tenderness.
usage.zh: 常见于“儿女情长，英雄气短”。略带批评，也可指柔情。

natural: vast in volumes and book-wraps

meaning.en: Describes a huge number of books or a work of many volumes.
meaning.zh: 形容书籍或文献卷数极多。

examples.zh: 这部百科全书卷帙浩繁。
examples.en: This encyclopedia is vast.

examples.zh: 古籍卷帙浩繁，整理起来十分困难。
examples.en: Ancient texts are so voluminous that cataloguing them is hard.

examples.zh: 面对卷帙浩繁的史料，他整整读了三年。
examples.en: Faced with a vast body of historical material, he spent three years reading it.

usage.en: Literary; 帙 is zhì ('book wrapper'), often written wrongly as 秩. Usually attributive or predicate.
usage.zh: 书面语；“帙”读 zhì，指书套，常被误写为“秩”。作定语、谓语。

natural: restrain oneself and return to ritual propriety

meaning.en: To discipline oneself and act in accordance with proper conduct.
meaning.zh: 约束自己，使言行符合礼制。

examples.zh: 孔子说，克己复礼为仁。
examples.en: Confucius said that restraining oneself and returning to ritual is humaneness.

examples.zh: 他一生克己复礼，从不逾矩。
examples.en: All his life he exercised restraint and never overstepped the rules.

examples.zh: 领导干部要克己复礼，严守纪律。
examples.en: Officials must discipline themselves and observe regulations strictly.

story.en: Yan Hui asks about humaneness, and Confucius replies that to restrain oneself and return to ritual is humaneness.

usage.en: Formal; 己 is jǐ ('self'), not 已. Often quoted from the Analects.
usage.zh: 较正式；“己”读 jǐ，不是“已”。常引自《论语》。

natural: burning bean stalks to cook beans

meaning.en: Relatives hurting each other; infighting among brothers.
meaning.zh: 烧豆秆煮豆子；比喻兄弟骨肉互相残害。

equivalents: family members turning on each other

examples.zh: 兄弟为争家产对簿公堂，真是煮豆燃萁。
examples.en: Brothers fighting in court over inheritance, a real case of kin turning on kin.

examples.zh: 同行之间煮豆燃萁，只会让对手得利。
examples.en: Infighting among peers only benefits rivals.

examples.zh: 煮豆燃萁的悲剧不应再重演。
examples.en: The tragedy of relatives turning on each other should not be repeated.

story.en: Cao Pi ordered his brother Cao Zhi to compose a poem within seven steps or be executed; Cao Zhi wrote of beans weeping in the pot while stalks burned beneath, 'born of the same root, why such haste to cook me?'.
story.zh: 曹植七步成诗：“煮豆持作羹，漉菽以为汁。萁在釜下燃，豆在釜中泣。本是同根生，相煎何太急？”

usage.en: Derogatory, literary; a version of the 'seven-step poem' story. 萁 is qí. Often cited with 相煎何急.
usage.zh: 贬义，书面语；出自“七步诗”的故事。“萁”读 qí。常与“相煎何急”并用。

natural: the skill of slaying dragons

meaning.en: A great skill with no practical use.
meaning.zh: 精妙却没有实际用处的本领。

examples.zh: 学了一身屠龙之技，却找不到工作。
examples.en: He mastered a skill nobody needs and couldn't find a job.

examples.zh: 这些理论只是屠龙之技，脱离实际。
examples.en: These theories are impressive but have no practical use.

examples.zh: 不要只练屠龙之技，要学能用的本事。
examples.en: Don't only train in impractical skills; learn useful ones.

story.en: Zhu Pingman spent three years and a fortune learning to slay dragons from Zhili Yi, but then could find no use for his skill.
story.zh: 《庄子·列御寇》：“朱泙漫学屠龙于支离益，殚千金之家，三年技成而无所用其巧。”

usage.en: Mild criticism or self-mockery, about knowledge without application. Often a joke about postgraduate studies. Predicate or object.
usage.zh: 轻微批评或自嘲，指学而无用的本领；常拿来调侃高深却冷门的专业。作谓语、宾语。

natural: losing a sheep at a fork in the road

meaning.en: With too many choices or too complicated a subject, one loses one's way and gets nowhere.
meaning.zh: 岔路太多，丢了羊；比喻事物复杂多变，没有正确方向就会迷失。

equivalents: going astray with no clear direction

examples.zh: 学习方向太多，难免歧路亡羊。
examples.en: With too many directions to study, one easily goes astray.

examples.zh: 创业者缺乏重点，容易歧路亡羊。
examples.en: Entrepreneurs without focus can easily get lost.

examples.zh: 治学要专，不然会歧路亡羊。
examples.en: In study one must focus, or one gets lost.

story.en: Yang Zhu's neighbour lost a sheep and many went to search, but the road had many forks and the sheep could not be found; Yang Zhu grew sad, saying so it is with the truth.
story.zh: 杨子之邻人亡羊，众人追之，歧路之中又有歧焉，不知所之。

usage.en: Warning about lack of focus; 亡 is wáng here ('lose'). Also found as 多歧亡羊.
usage.zh: 提醒做事要有重点；“亡”读 wáng，意为丢失。也说“多歧亡羊”。

natural: one meal repaid with a thousand in gold

meaning.en: To repay even a small kindness generously.
meaning.zh: 受人一餐之恩，以千金报答；比喻厚报恩人。

examples.zh: 他一饭千金，成功后重金酬谢当年的恩人。
examples.en: He repaid his benefactor handsomely after he succeeded.

examples.zh: 一饭千金的故事教人懂得感恩。
examples.en: The story of the meal repaid with gold teaches gratitude.

examples.zh: 她有一饭千金的气度，从不忘记别人的好。
examples.en: She is generous in returning favours and never forgets kindnesses.

story.en: The poor Han Xin was fed by a washerwoman for days; once he became Prince of Chu he found her and gave her a thousand in gold.
story.zh: 韩信贫时受漂母饭食，后封楚王，“赐漂母千金”。

usage.en: Praise; points to Han Xin's story. Often used about gratitude rather than extravagance.
usage.zh: 褒义，典出韩信；多指知恩图报，而非挥霍。

natural: a talent unmatched in the land

meaning.en: A person of talent with no equal in the country.
meaning.zh: 国内独一无二的杰出人才。

examples.zh: 在科学界，他堪称国士无双。
examples.en: In science he is a peerless talent.

examples.zh: 当年人们称赞他国士无双。
examples.en: In his day people praised him as unmatched in the land.

examples.zh: 她的才华国士无双，无人能比。
examples.en: Her talent is unrivalled in the nation.

story.en: Xiao He urged Liu Bang to keep Han Xin, saying generals are easy to find but a talent like Han Xin is unmatched in the whole land.
story.zh: 萧何对刘邦说：“诸将易得耳；至如信者，国士无双。”

usage.en: Strong praise; refers to Han Xin, as recommended by Xiao He. Used for outstanding talent, not for warfare only.
usage.zh: 高度赞美，典出萧何称赞韩信；泛指杰出人才，不限于军事。

natural: an old ox licking its calf

meaning.en: Parental love, as an old ox lovingly licks its calf.
meaning.zh: 老牛舔小牛；比喻父母疼爱子女。

examples.zh: 看到女儿远行，他老牛舐犊般地叮嘱个不停。
examples.en: Seeing his daughter off, he kept fussing over her with a parent's love.

examples.zh: 父亲对孩子的爱，就像老牛舐犊。
examples.en: A father's love for his child is like an old ox for its calf.

examples.zh: 老牛舐犊的深情，孩子往往到长大才明白。
examples.en: Children often only understand a parent's deep love when they are grown.

story.en: Cao Cao had Yang Xiu killed and, seeing Yang Xiu's father Yang Biao grown thin, asked why; Yang Biao answered that he felt shame at lacking foresight, and was like an old ox with its love for a calf.
story.zh: 杨彪答曹操：“愧无日磾先见之明，犹怀老牛舐犊之爱。”

usage.en: Warm; describes parent love, mostly of fathers and mothers in later life. The variants 舐犊情深 and 舐犊之爱 are also used. 舐 is shì.
usage.zh: 温馨褒义，形容父母对子女的爱；变体“舐犊情深”“舐犊之爱”也常用。“舐”读 shì。

natural: Sichuan dogs barking at the sun

meaning.en: To be astonished by what is ordinary because one has seen little of the world.
meaning.zh: 四川的狗见到太阳就叫；比喻少见多怪。

examples.zh: 没见过高铁就大惊小怪，简直是蜀犬吠日。
examples.en: Marvelling at the high-speed train as if it were a miracle is like the dogs of Shu barking at the sun.

examples.zh: 别蜀犬吠日了，这只是常见技术。
examples.en: Don't make a fuss; this is a common technology.

examples.zh: 他对新事物的惊讶，让人想到蜀犬吠日。
examples.en: His surprise at new things brings to mind Sichuan dogs barking at the sun.

origin.source: 柳宗元《答韦中立论师道书》

story.en: Liu Zongyuan writes that in Shu the hills are high and mist heavy, the sun seldom seen, so when it comes out the dogs bark at it.
story.zh: 柳宗元《答韦中立论师道书》：“蜀中山高雾重，见日时稀，每至日出，则群犬吠之。”

usage.en: Mocking; 蜀 = Sichuan. Close to 少见多怪 but more literary. Predicate or object.
usage.zh: 带嘲讽；“蜀”指四川。与“少见多怪”近，但更书面。作谓语、宾语。

natural: mistaking 鲁 for 鱼 and 亥 for 豕

meaning.en: Errors in copying or printing texts, from characters that look alike.
meaning.zh: 把“鲁”写成“鱼”，把“亥”写成“豕”；指书籍在传抄、刊印中的文字错误。

examples.zh: 古籍传抄多次，难免鲁鱼亥豕。
examples.en: After many copyings of ancient texts, errors are inevitable.

examples.zh: 校对要仔细，以免出现鲁鱼亥豕之误。
examples.en: Proofread carefully to avoid typos and misprints.

examples.zh: 这个版本鲁鱼亥豕不少，不宜引用。
examples.en: This edition has many copying errors and shouldn't be cited.

story.en: In the Lüshi Chunqiu, 'Ji Hai crossed the river' was miscopied as 'three pigs crossed the river'; the Baopuzi says that after three copyings, 'Lu' becomes 'fish'.
story.zh: 《吕氏春秋·察传》：“己亥涉河”误成“三豕涉河”；《抱朴子》：“书三写，鲁成鱼，虚成虎。”

usage.en: Literary, used of textual editing and proofreading. Also written 亥豕鲁鱼. 亥 is hài ('boar' in the zodiac), 豕 shǐ ('pig').
usage.zh: 书面语，用于校勘、校对。也作“亥豕鲁鱼”。“亥”读 hài，“豕”读 shǐ。
